why: Count palindromic substrings by position (equal strings at different places count separately). Every palindrome has a centre, so expanding around each of the 2n-1 centres, or Manacher's radii, counts them all.
hints: Each palindrome is symmetric around a centre: a letter (odd length) or a gap between two letters (even length). How many centres are there?
From each centre, expand outward while the characters match; every successful step is one more palindrome. Manacher's algorithm reuses mirror information to get every radius in linear time.
Expand-around-centre is O(n^2) worst case and fine for moderate n; Manacher gives O(n): answer = sum over centres of the number of palindromes (radius) at that centre.
pitfalls: Equal substrings at different positions count separately: "ll" appears twice in "hellolle" and counts as 2.
Remember even-length centres (between letters), or "ll" and "lloll" are missed.
Single letters each count as a palindrome.
constraints:
• Bounds are not stated in the source. Reasonable: 1 <= |s| <= 10^5 (O(n^2) expansion is fine up to a few thousand)
  • s contains only lowercase English letters
